answer:
Training uses statistics over batch and spatial dimensions for each channel. Normalize with the population variance, but update running_var with its unbiased correction, matching PyTorch’s convention. Evaluation uses running buffers and never recomputes batch statistics. Momentum is the new-statistic weight in the EMA, not optimizer momentum. A training channel with only one observation cannot provide the unbiased running variance update.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** Batch normalization uses $\hat x=(x-\mu_B)/\sqrt{v_B+\epsilon}$ and $y=\gamma\hat x+\beta$. A running estimate updates as $r_{new}=(1-m)r_{old}+mr_B$ under PyTorch's momentum convention. Because examples share training statistics, splitting a batch into microbatches generally changes the forward computation even when gradients are accumulated later. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.03167)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://theaisummer.com/normalization/) and [2](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.BatchNorm1d.html).
